subtype: Approach: making a guest list with a limit on numbers [Thinking]
passage:
Shankar: Mummy, I want the whole class at my party. That's thirty-four.
Mummy: The flat holds fifteen, my clever boy, counting cousins.
Shankar: Fifteen. Hmm. Let me write. Cousins first: Gurpreet, Neha, Ravi, Kabir. Four. Then friends I play with every day. Eight, nine... nineteen in all.
Mummy: That is four too many.
Shankar: I know. If I cut the ones I only sit near in class, those are four names. The people who matter most stay. It feels bad, but nobody can come to a cramped party anyway.
Gurpreet: Am I in?
Shankar: You're the first one on the list.

qa.q: How many people can the flat hold for the party?
qa.a: The flat holds fifteen, counting cousins.

qa.q: How does Shankar feel about cutting names from the list?
qa.a: Shankar feels sorry and a bit sad about it, since he says "It feels bad," but he accepts it because a cramped party would not be fun for anyone.

qa.q: What other approach could Shankar try, and why?
qa.a: Shankar could ask if the whole class could join a small outing later, since more friends can be included without crowding the flat. Sharing a treat at school could also work.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet feel when asking whether an invitation is coming?
qa.a: Gurpreet is probably nervous and hopeful, since Gurpreet asks aloud and is glad to hear the name is first on the list.

grounding: A boy told the flat holds only fifteen counts the names, puts cousins and close friends first and cuts a few.

subtype: Approach: making a guest list with a limit on numbers [Thinking]
passage: When I turned eleven, I wanted my whole class of thirty-eight at the party. Amma said our flat could fit fifteen, including cousins. That night I sat with a notebook and thought it through. First: who would I be sad without? Pema, obviously, and my cricket team, six of them. Then the cousins, four, because Amma said so and because I like them. Eleven. Then my bench partner, the two boys from tuition, and Kiran, who lent me his bat. Fifteen. Then I remembered Arvind. Sixteen. I sat for a long time. Arvind I only talk to at lunch. I crossed him out and felt a bit mean. Amma read the list and said, 'Harsha, my boy, that's a good list.'

qa.q: How many people could the flat fit?
How did Harsha feel when he crossed Arvind out?
qa.a: Harsha felt a bit mean and torn, but decided a lunch-time classmate mattered less than those already on the list.

qa.q: What else could Harsha do for classmates he couldn't invite?
qa.a: Share sweets with the whole class at school so nobody feels completely left out; the list itself was fair because he started with who mattered most.

qa.q: How might Amma see Harsha's list?
qa.a: Amma sees he kept to fifteen and chose carefully, so she is pleased and calls it a good list.

grounding: Shows a boy limited to fifteen guests listing close friends and cousins first, counting, and cutting one to keep to the number.

subtype: Approach: making a guest list with a limit on numbers [Thinking]
passage: Note left for Ammu on the fridge, Saturday. While you were at work, Tanvir sat at the dining table for an hour with his party list. He wanted to ask all thirty of his class. I said fifteen is our limit; this flat can't hold more. He didn't argue. He wrote cousins first, five of them, then his closest friends, starting with Gurleen. He counted: seventeen. He looked at it a long time, then crossed out two boys from his van, saying, 'I only see them in the van.' He was quiet after that. I told him we'll send extra sweets for the van. Please look at his list tonight. Abbu

qa.q: How many names were on Tanvir's first count?
How did Tanvir seem to feel after crossing out the two boys?
qa.a: He was quiet, which suggests he felt a bit sad or guilty about leaving them out.

qa.q: What else could help Tanvir feel better about the cut?
qa.a: Sending extra sweets for the van, as Abbu suggested, so the two boys still feel remembered.

qa.q: How does Abbu see the way Tanvir made the list?
qa.a: Abbu notices Tanvir accepted the limit without arguing and chose carefully, and wants Ammu to see the list too.

grounding: Illustrates a boy with a fifteen-guest limit listing cousins and close friends first, counting, and cutting two to fit.
